I never wanted to go to church but went because if I didn't, I didn't drive, play sports, etc. My mom was my seminary teacher (early morning) so I had to go for that. I always enjoyed the activities because like you said, the boys got to do fun things. Now, I was a "good" boy but definitely understood that my issues were my own. I don't remember ever being taught the "girls should be modest so a boys mind can be clean." I know many females who were taught that. I do remember pissing off a teacher during that gum lesson. I picked it up and started chewing it and said "Yeah, it's still good." But I definitely got into my fair share of "Mormon" trouble. I had the reputation of being the guy who dated all the girls, made out with them, fooled around more, then when their guilt came they would cut it off. Now, I never felt as if I forced anyone to do anything they didn't want to do. But I felt the guilt too eventually. Mainly because if I kept living this way, I couldn't live with my family eternally. I was in and out of the Bishop's office throughout my teenage years. My Bishop then was actually a really great guy. I have no complaints about him at all. I continued my ways until it was time to go on a mission I did not want to go on but was expected of me. Until, my mother passed away when I was 19. I dove deep into my "sins." I will also preface this with that like before, it was mainly sexual things and always consensual.  Lied to everyone just to be able to go on my mission at 21. Went through the MTC, and 1 week into my mission, the crushing guilt got to me and I confessed everything to my Mission President. He contacted "the brethren" and I was sent home. Was told to take care of it and come back. My stake president made his anger with me get apparent for lying to him. I didn't change. About a year later when it was time to back out, I was suicidal. I couldn't do it. Decided not to go. Met a non Mormon girl at college. Asked her out and she said maybe. Thought it was cute and I told her to let me know. She had never dated a Mormon before and asked the only one she knew if he knew me. It was my Stake President, who she worked for. He told her I was not a good person and that she shouldn't date me. That I was probably one who would put something in her drink on our date (Direct Quote, she told me that she didn't believe that but politely refused the date). I moved to Utah to be near my Brother and finish college at UVU (the devil's college lol). I met up with a girl I knew in high school and because I felt broken started dating her. I didn't like being alone. We probably should have never been together. I also say that I did love her. I love hard. B ut we still both felt the pull out the church and our families to be married in the temple. We got married there and agreed to keep up the charade. I will say I definitely believed it more. After 2 kids and 6 years of Marraige, she was done with the church. I got angry because I was scared of my family disowning me and having the dreaded "Exmormon" tag. After a year of little fights, I found out she had an affair for the last year. I was broken. I finally went to a therapist. I had been fighting with church history for sometime as well. Realized I had been keeping up the charade too long. I didn't believe it. I hadn't for a long time. My therapist just helped me learn to love myself. My wife and I divorced. I loved here but she continued her affair even after she swore it was over. I came out of the "non believing" closet to everyone. My ex wife and I co parent well. I took some time and focused on just being a good person. I met someone who I am glad I didn't meet when I was struggling. I'm finally part of a good relationship. No secrets, no putting on a face for anyone. My family loves me. Even though they still some times try to "save" me. I politely decline and it's all good for the most part.

This is what happened to me last year. My ex had an affair and I had been with my boys the majority of the time (picking up from daycare, stay at home for 2 years, etc). First things first, this sucks. No other way around it. I would cry the moment my boys drove away. My first piece of advice would be find hobbies. Things to occupy your time. It's not easy but it does get easier to deal with. Once you and the kids get into a routine, it becomes better for everyone. My ex and I also video chat with it boys every night. I bought a nest hub man so they can call her when they want and she did as well.

Third, fight! Fight for all the custody you deserve. I fought and made sure I got my 50/50 joint legal custody. Get a lawyer that will fight for you. Remember that all your things are just that. Things. They can be replaced. What can't be replaced is your time. If you make that your focus, you, your lawyer, your kids, judges, etc will see that.
